solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Doctor put into a group round hospital with many others

indicators.note: the grouping word goes round the hospital letter, enclosing it

parts.note: banded together, formed into a band

explanation.surface: A doctor is moved into a hospital team alongside many colleagues.
explanation.walkthrough: MO + B(H)ANDED gives MOB-HANDED.
explanation.definitionFit: Mob-handed describes doing something in a large crowd, accompanied by plenty of other people.

clue.text: Slowly transform school party going over hotel

indicators.note: in a down clue, going over suggests flipping the word upwards, so it reads backwards

parts.note: a prom is a school dance
H is hotel in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: A school party travels across to a hotel.
explanation.definitionFit: To morph is to change gradually from one shape into another, as in animation effects.

clue.text: Literary castle often veiled

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the great house in Evelyn Waugh's novel ... Revisited
second meaning, read as two words: the head of a woman at her wedding, usually covered by a veil

explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as BRIDE'S HEAD for the second, playful meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: Waugh's novel centres on a grand country house; a woman marrying traditionally wears a veil over her face and hair.

clue.text: A monarch abandoning modern art, rejected as without purpose

indicators.note: something rejected is sent back, so what remains is read the other way
the monarch walks away from the art phrase, so those letters are taken out of it

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword's usual monarch

explanation.surface: A king or queen walks away from a contemporary gallery, dismissing it all as pointless.
explanation.walkthrough: The monarch is taken out of the two-word phrase, not from just one letter; what is left turns round and follows A.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something at random means acting haphazardly, with no plan, aim or method behind it.

clue.text: Refuse Duke Lawrence

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for duke
T E Lawrence served in the RAF under the name Ross

explanation.surface: A duke turns down Lawrence.
explanation.walkthrough: Refuse is the noun (rubbish), not the verb it seems.
explanation.definitionFit: Dross is worthless waste matter, originally the scum skimmed from molten metal.

clue.text: Philosopher taking sort of lead, with children round about

indicators.note: the offspring word takes in the cable word, holding it inside
turned round about means facing the other way, so the offspring word is read backwards

parts.note: seed is an old word for offspring
a SCART lead is a cable connecting TV and video equipment

explanation.surface: A thinker picks up some kind of cable while the kids gather round.
explanation.walkthrough: DEES (SEED reversed) takes in SCART: DE(SCART)ES.
explanation.definitionFit: René Descartes was the seventeenth-century French thinker famous for 'I think, therefore I am'.

clue.text: One who's not genuine scarecrow

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a sham or front person, someone of no substance
second meaning: a stuffed figure put in fields to frighten birds

explanation.walkthrough: A scarecrow is literally a figure of a person stuffed with straw.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is used for a person set up as a sham, and literally fits the stuffed field figure.

clue.text: Paste is inserted by doctor

indicators.note: the little word is put inside the doctor's letters

explanation.surface: A doctor applies some paste.
explanation.definitionFit: Miso is a Japanese fermented soybean paste used to flavour soups and sauces.

clue.text: Properly fixed, having got worse after November

indicators.note: this sets the order: the sickness word comes behind the letter for November

parts.note: N is November in the NATO alphabet
ailed means fell ill or deteriorated

explanation.surface: Something repaired has deteriorated since November.
explanation.definitionFit: If something is nailed it is securely fastened, or colloquially pinned down or achieved perfectly.

clue.text: Paper money minister initially covered in restrictions

parts.note: financial means to do with money

indicators.note: that letter is enclosed by the word for restrictions
only the opening letter of the government word is wanted

explanation.surface: A finance minister finds their plans hemmed in by rules.
explanation.walkthrough: FINANCIAL + TI(M)ES.
explanation.definitionFit: The Financial Times is a British daily newspaper famous for its pink pages and business coverage.

clue.text: Delivered curve ball, perhaps, got very upset

definitions.meaning: first meaning, literal: pitched a ball that wobbles in flight
second meaning: had a tantrum

explanation.walkthrough: To throw a wobbly is British slang for losing your temper; the first part reads it literally as a bowler's swerving delivery.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means flying into a rage or panic, losing composure in a dramatic tantrum.

clue.text: In a Med island clubs grow together

indicators.note: the clubs letter is placed inside the island's name

parts.note: Crete is a Greek island in the Mediterranean
C is clubs in card notation

explanation.surface: On a Mediterranean island, golf clubs or nightclubs are sprouting up together.
explanation.walkthrough: A + C(C)RETE.
explanation.definitionFit: To accrete is to grow by gradual accumulation, layers sticking on and merging over time.

clue.text: Wheatear chewed and eaten by senior bird

indicators.note: the mangled letters go inside the abbreviation for senior

parts.note: SR is the abbreviation for senior

indicators.note: something chewed is mangled out of its original form, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: One small bird is mauled and devoured by a bigger, older one.
explanation.walkthrough: A wheatear is itself a bird, so the surface is a bird-eat-bird scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Shearwaters are long-winged seabirds that skim low over the waves, as in the Manx variety.

clue.text: Runner arrives in haste at start of relay

indicators.note: the arrival abbreviation sits inside the old word for hurry

parts.note: hie is an old verb meaning to hurry
ARR is the timetable abbreviation for arrives

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the final word is taken

explanation.surface: An athlete dashes in hurriedly to begin a relay leg.
explanation.walkthrough: H(ARR)IE + R.
explanation.definitionFit: A harrier is a cross-country runner; many athletics clubs are named Harriers.

clue.text: Meeting of alumni? There's a thing

parts.note: OB is old boy, a former pupil
a session is a sitting or gathering

explanation.surface: A reunion of former pupils is apparently something special.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as an old boys' session: OB + SESSION.
explanation.definitionFit: To have a thing about something is to be fixated on it, which is what an obsession is.

clue.text: One page coming out of directory

indicators.note: the answer emerges from within the letters of the next word

parts.note: the middle letters of this word

explanation.surface: A page is pulled from a phone book.
explanation.definitionFit: The recto is the right-hand page of an open book, the front of a leaf.

clue.text: Excessive lavender and rosemary at first in round border

indicators.note: those letters are placed within the edge word

parts.note: a verge is a grass edge

indicators.note: only the opening letters of the three plant-related words are used

explanation.surface: Too much lavender and rosemary has been planted in a circular flowerbed.
explanation.walkthrough: O + VER(LAR)GE. The 'and' supplies its A too.
explanation.definitionFit: Overlarge means too big, of excessive size, which is what excessive conveys.

clue.text: A quiet period assembling for a fast start

indicators.note: the pieces named before it are put together one after another

parts.note: sh is a call for quiet
a day of the week is a period of time, defined by example

explanation.surface: A short silent spell gathers people for a quick start.
explanation.walkthrough: The fast is Lent, not speed: this day begins it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ash Wednesday is the first day of Lent, the forty-day Christian season of fasting.

clue.text: Receive two presents but not make further advance

parts.note: now is the present time, here the present place

explanation.surface: Someone gets two gifts yet still makes no progress.
explanation.walkthrough: Presents means present time and present place, not gifts: NOW + HERE.
explanation.definitionFit: To get nowhere is to fail to progress, making no headway at all.

clue.text: Not so much needed to cover girl, being thin

indicators.note: the comparative word wraps around the girl's name

explanation.surface: A slimmer girl needs less to cover herself.
explanation.walkthrough: LE(ANNE)SS.
explanation.definitionFit: Leanness is the state of having little fat, i.e. the condition of being slim.

clue.text: Old police supervisors choosing what to close round wrists?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the local council bodies that once oversaw British borough police forces

definitions.text: choosing what to close round wrists?
definitions.meaning: second meaning, whimsical: a panel selecting a timepiece to strap on

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the jokey second reading: a committee picking a wristwatch.
explanation.definitionFit: Watch committees were council committees that controlled municipal police forces in England until 1964.

clue.text: Sensational preoccupation about running water

indicators.note: the fixation word goes round the stream word

parts.note: a rill is a small brook

explanation.surface: A sensational fixation with flowing water.
explanation.walkthrough: TH(RILL)ING.
explanation.definitionFit: Thrilling means causing excitement, exactly as something sensational does.

clue.text: Crazed drummer's means of transport

parts.note: Keith Moon was the drummer of The Who

explanation.surface: A drummer's vehicle has gone mad.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as MOON'S TRUCK; Moon himself was famously wild.
explanation.definitionFit: Moonstruck means mentally unbalanced, from the old belief that the moon caused madness.

clue.text: Fair experience very popular with creep

parts.note: a big hit is very popular
a heel is a contemptible person

explanation.surface: A well-liked creep runs a fair.
explanation.walkthrough: Fair is the funfair, not justice.
explanation.definitionFit: A big wheel is a giant Ferris wheel ride found at fairgrounds.

clue.text: Nursing leg, shot — by him?

indicators.note: something shot is wrecked, so these letters are thrown into new order

explanation.surface: A wounded man tends his leg, having been shot by a gunman.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: the shooter of a cowboy film.
explanation.definitionFit: A gunslinger is a Wild West gunfighter, the person who would have fired the shot.

clue.text: Defector from Scottish party returning her dress?

indicators.note: coming back means going the opposite way, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: a Nat is a member of the Scottish Nationalists

explanation.surface: A turncoat leaves the Scottish Nationalists and gives back her outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: Each short word is turned round separately, defector first. The 'her' and question mark hint at a Scottish woman's dress.
explanation.definitionFit: Tartan is the checked woollen cloth of Highland dress, so a Scottish lady might wear it.

clue.text: Politician tending to arouse lecherous thoughts, by agreement

parts.note: sensual means suggestive of physical pleasure

explanation.surface: A seductive politician, but everyone agrees to it.
explanation.definitionFit: Consensual means done with the consent of all parties, which is what by agreement means.

clue.text: Violinist, say, during and at the end of recital?

definitions.text: Violinist, say, during and at the end of recital?

parts.words: Violinist, say, during and at the end of recital?
parts.note: surface reading: a string player performing a concert

parts.words: during and at the end of recital?
parts.note: setter's reading: someone who uses a bow while playing and then takes a bow at the end

explanation.walkthrough: The two senses of bow, drawing it across strings and bending at the waist, both fit one performer.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means one who bows, and a violinist does that both with the instrument and to applause.

clue.text: What everyone supports the tiniest bit: government

indicators.note: in a down clue, supporting means standing underneath, so these come after

parts.note: a whit is the smallest amount
eh is a request to repeat

explanation.surface: Everybody backs the state's smallest measure.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue the 'What everyone' pieces sit under the tiniest bit, and 'What' is the exclamation of someone who missed what was said.
explanation.definitionFit: Whitehall, the London street of ministries, is shorthand for the British civil service and government.

clue.text: No atmosphere? I'm having to change double act

indicators.note: the preceding words must alter their order

explanation.surface: A performer complains the show lacks atmosphere and must be reworked.
explanation.walkthrough: A pantomime horse is a British Christmas-show costume worn by two actors.
explanation.definitionFit: Two performers share the costume, front legs and back legs, so it is literally a double act.

clue.text: Go over and over something on the drums

definitions.meaning: first meaning: turn repeatedly
second meaning: a rapid continuous drumbeat

explanation.definitionFit: To roll is to turn over repeatedly; a drum roll is a fast sustained beat on a drum.

clue.text: Heavily defeat male, since all but untouchable

indicators.note: everything except the final letter is kept

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for male

explanation.surface: A man is roundly beaten because he is nearly sacrosanct.
explanation.definitionFit: In sport a massacre is a crushing win, so to massacre is to trounce an opponent.

clue.text: Made manure as temperature dropped in calm

indicators.note: the letter for temperature is let fall out of the word

parts.note: T is the symbol for temperature

explanation.surface: Someone made compost when it got cooler.
explanation.definitionFit: Composed means self-possessed and serene, which is to say calm.

clue.text: Even biography is an art form

parts.note: as in still better, even better

explanation.surface: Even writing a biography counts as art.
explanation.definitionFit: Still life is a genre of painting depicting inanimate objects like fruit and flowers.

clue.text: Paste up a brunette, top of torso retouched

indicators.note: a picture retouched is altered, so the letters are rearranged
only the head letter of the body word is used

explanation.surface: A pin-up photo of a dark-haired model has the upper body touched up.
explanation.definitionFit: Peanut butter is a spread made from ground roasted peanuts, a smooth or crunchy paste.

clue.text: This term oddly tires me out

indicators.note: the first, third and so on letters are taken
the words before it are put out of order

explanation.surface: A student groans that this school term exhausts them.
explanation.walkthrough: Term does double duty, in the definition and as the source of its odd letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A trimester is one of three terms in an academic year, or a three-month period.

clue.text: Not to be touched on behind, daughter ordered

parts.note: tabu is a variant spelling of taboo
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A daughter is told not to touch her behind.
explanation.definitionFit: Tabulated means arranged in tables, set out in an orderly systematic form.

clue.text: Inopportune fret by half back

parts.note: a fret is a sea fog on the coast of north-east England

indicators.note: going back means the half word is read the other way

parts.note: demi is a prefix meaning half

explanation.surface: Worrying about a half-back's poor timing.
explanation.walkthrough: Fret looks like worry and half back like a football position; neither is.
explanation.definitionFit: Mistimed describes something done at the wrong moment, i.e. at an inopportune time.

clue.text: Manages to drop daughter in marshland

indicators.note: the abbreviation for daughter is let go from the word

parts.note: fends, as in fends for oneself
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A parent manages to drop off their daughter in a marsh.
explanation.walkthrough: The Fens are low-lying wetlands of eastern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Fens are areas of low wet ground, the boggy marshland of East Anglia being the best known.

clue.text: Inch round close to the blue delta, not across the bay?

indicators.note: the creeping word goes round the following pieces

parts.note: to sidle is to edge along

indicators.note: the final letter of the next word is wanted

parts.note: D is delta in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: Edging round a blue river delta rather than crossing the bay by boat.
explanation.walkthrough: SID(E SAD D)LE. The bay is a brown horse: riding sidesaddle means not sitting astride it.
explanation.definitionFit: Riding sidesaddle means sitting with both legs on one side of the horse, not straddling it.

clue.text: At home, box inlaid with pine missing its top — turn to ash

indicators.note: the shortened wood goes inside the box word
the tree word loses its first letter

explanation.surface: A pine-inlaid box at home is burnt to ash.
explanation.walkthrough: IN + C(INE)RATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To incinerate is to burn something completely, reducing it to ashes.

clue.text: Get cracking, say, to open container

indicators.note: the example abbreviation goes into the container word to open it up

explanation.surface: Someone is told to get on and open a box.
explanation.walkthrough: B(EG)IN.
explanation.definitionFit: To get cracking means to start doing something promptly, so to begin.

clue.text: Plant second holy book (good!) in church

indicators.note: the book and the good letter go inside the abbreviation for the church

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: A second holy book, a good one, is planted in church.
explanation.walkthrough: MO + C(KORAN G)E.
explanation.definitionFit: Mock orange is a shrub, philadelphus, with fragrant white flowers smelling like orange blossom.

clue.text: Stalin as a vicious aggressor

indicators.note: something vicious is savage and wild, so the letters before it are thrown about

explanation.surface: The Soviet dictator was a brutal attacker.
explanation.definitionFit: An assailant is someone who attacks another person, the one taking the aggressive role.

clue.text: Presumably happy about one omitted from speech

indicators.note: the cheerful word goes around the numeral

parts.note: if not sad, presumably happy: a made-up word
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone apparently cheerful about one thing left out of an address.
explanation.walkthrough: UNS(I)AD. The question of whether unsad is a word is why the clue says presumably.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unsaid is left unspoken, not voiced, i.e. kept out of what was said aloud.

clue.text: Not mentally sound, take horse out?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: psychologically unbalanced
second meaning, whimsical: to remove from its stall, like unsaddle

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a coined verb: if you can stable a horse, you might un-stable it.
explanation.definitionFit: Unstable describes a mind prone to sudden changes, and jokily means removing a horse from its stall.

clue.text: Searching for this, Marcel fell behind

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Proust's novel In Search of ...
second meaning: was delayed, slipped back

explanation.walkthrough: Marcel is Marcel Proust, whose great novel's English title is In Search of Lost Time.
explanation.definitionFit: Proust's narrator seeks the past; a runner or project that lost time dropped behind schedule.

clue.text: Set of dishes for ceremony

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a matching dinner set
second meaning: a religious rite

explanation.surface: A table set out for a formal occasion.
explanation.definitionFit: A dinner service is a full set of matching crockery; a church service is a religious ceremony.

clue.text: Illnesses later devastated island group

indicators.note: the words before it are laid waste and left in a new order

explanation.surface: Diseases later ravage a chain of islands.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lesser Antilles are the arc of small Caribbean islands running from the Virgin Islands to Trinidad.

clue.text: Good-time girl's sort of infection

parts.note: gal is a casual word for a girl

explanation.surface: A party girl has caught some infection.
explanation.definitionFit: A fungal infection, such as athlete's foot or thrush, is one caused by a fungus.

clue.text: Summarily dismissed in speech all the time

indicators.note: the words are to be heard spoken, not seen written

explanation.surface: Someone was abruptly sacked for talking all the time.
explanation.definitionFit: Throughout means for the whole duration, from start to finish, which is all the time.

clue.text: Current situation of the national myth?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the state of affairs
second meaning, playful: a falsehood belonging to the country

explanation.walkthrough: Read the phrase literally: a lie (myth) of the land (nation).
explanation.definitionFit: The lie of the land is the way things currently stand, originally the shape of the terrain.

clue.text: Stranger backing Communist Party

indicators.note: going backwards, so the political pair is read in reverse

explanation.surface: An outsider is supporting the Communist Party.
explanation.walkthrough: Stranger is the comparative adjective, more strange, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: Odder means more peculiar, the comparative of odd, which is what stranger also is.

clue.text: President commonly received a text

indicators.note: common speech drops the aitch at the front of the word

explanation.surface: A president gets a text message.
explanation.definitionFit: John Adams and his son John Quincy Adams were the second and sixth US presidents.

clue.text: Hollywood figure perhaps, half naked

indicators.note: only the first half of the slang word is kept

parts.note: starkers is British slang for naked

explanation.surface: A film celebrity appears half-undressed.
explanation.definitionFit: A star is a celebrated performer, and a Hollywood film star is the typical example.

clue.text: Meaning to float along

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the gist
second meaning: be carried by a current

explanation.walkthrough: Meaning to looks like intending to, but the two halves are separate senses.
explanation.definitionFit: The drift of an argument is its general sense; to drift is to be borne passively on water or air.

clue.text: Principally relied on such a drive in a British vehicle

definitions.meaning: first meaning: most trusted

definitions.text: such a drive in a British vehicle
definitions.meaning: second meaning: with the steering wheel on that side

explanation.walkthrough: British cars are built with the steering wheel on the side away from the kerb, because traffic keeps left.
explanation.definitionFit: A right-hand man is a chief helper; right-hand drive means the steering wheel sits on that side.

clue.text: One may be boring these days, joining in rough fight

indicators.note: the era abbreviation enters the fight word

parts.note: AD, anno Domini, is the present era

explanation.surface: These days a dull person still joins in a scrap.
explanation.walkthrough: Boring means making holes, not dull. BR(AD)AWL.
explanation.definitionFit: A bradawl is a small pointed hand tool for making holes in wood before screwing.

clue.text: "Where is the college porter?" barmaid said

indicators.note: spoken aloud, so the word is judged by its sound

explanation.surface: A barmaid is asked where a college's doorkeeper has gone.
explanation.walkthrough: Porter is the dark beer, not the college gatekeeper.
explanation.definitionFit: A beer cellar is the underground store where a college would keep its casks of porter.

clue.text: Setter chosen — assess regularly for brevity

indicators.note: the same cut, losing the first half, is made to each word in turn

explanation.surface: A crossword setter is selected to judge conciseness.
explanation.walkthrough: Each six-letter word gives up its first three letters, keeping only its second half.
explanation.definitionFit: Terseness is the quality of using few words, which is brevity in speech or writing.
